report_name: New Ransomware Group 'Emperador' Claims Attack on AB InBev

threat_actors.name: Emperador
threat_actors.description: A new ransomware group that appeared in September 2026, operating a double-extortion model. It claimed responsibility for the attack on AB InBev, exfiltrating 3.9 GB of data and demanding a $1 million ransom.

attack_patterns.name: Data from Cloud Storage Object
attack_patterns.description: The Emperador group claimed to have exfiltrated 3.2 GB of data from AB InBev's Azure blob storage assets.

attack_patterns.name: Private Keys
attack_patterns.description: The attackers claimed to have stolen internal Public Key Infrastructure (PKI) certificates, which could be used to sign malicious software or conduct man-in-the-middle attacks.

attack_patterns.name: Exfiltration Over Alternative Protocol
attack_patterns.description: The Emperador group exfiltrated 3.9 GB of sensitive data, including Azure blob storage assets and corporate emails, to their own infrastructure.

malware.name: Emperador Ransomware
malware.description: The ransomware associated with the Emperador group. The group's operations focus on a double-extortion model, exfiltrating data before potential encryption.

identities.name: Anheuser-Busch InBev
identities.description: The world's largest brewing company, targeted by the Emperador ransomware group. The group claimed to have exfiltrated 3.9 GB of data and demanded a $1 million ransom.

infrastructure.name: Emperador Leak Site
infrastructure.description: A dark web site used by the Emperador group to post claims of their attacks and threaten to leak stolen data from victims like AB InBev.

indicators.name: Potential Exfiltration of PKI Certificate Files
indicators.pattern:
title: Potential Exfiltration of PKI Certificate Files
id: 7c8b5d2a-1e3f-4b9c-8a7d-6f5e4d3c2b1a
status: experimental
description: Detects the creation of common private key file formats (.pfx, .p12, .pem), which could indicate staging for exfiltration as mentioned in the Emperador ransomware attack.
references:
  - https://rescana.com/post/emperador-ransomware-attack-analysis-ab-inbev-azure-cloud-data-breach-and-pki-certificate-exposure-october-2026
author: cyber.netsecops.io
date: 2026-10-27
tags:
  - attack.t1552.004
  - attack.credential_access
level: medium
logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetFilename|endswith:
      - '.pfx'
      - '.p12'
      - '.pem'
  filter_legit_path:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - 'C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Crypto\'
      - 'C:\Windows\System32\'
      - 'C:\Program Files\'
      - 'C:\Program Files (x86)\'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit_path
indicators.description: Detects the creation of files with extensions typical for PKI certificates (.pfx, .p12, .pem), which could indicate staging for exfiltration. The Emperador group was observed exfiltrating such certificates.

relationships.source_name: Potential Exfiltration of PKI Certificate Files
